response.answer: Your record supports saying that hotel-buffered travel is a risk-control measure, not a convenience: your only missed protocol deviation in six years occurred during a site audit the morning after a five-hour overnight drive, and a rested second monitor identified the finding the following week. Missed deviations are classified by the sponsor’s quality team as the most serious monitoring-failure category. The rebookings add about $300 per cycle, which you documented as small relative to that risk. It also supports distinguishing this from a general objection to demanding schedules: dense two-site days are workable when you have normal sleep. The record does not establish a universal guarantee that every hotel stop prevents an error, only this documented risk basis and cost rationale.
